title: NUSA Aves: Passive Bioacoustic Monitoring for Endangered Birds
summary: The second app. The first one needed a server to run the model, which is useless in a forest. This one runs the classifier on the phone itself, no connection required. Finalist at BRIN AIDeaNation 2026, 1 of 80 teams selected nationally.
highlights: Team leader and AI engineer: built the classifier, the inference server, and the CLI.
Re-architected from the earlier server-dependent app to on-device inference, so the classifier runs offline where the birds are rather than where the network is.
A recording is split into 3-second segments, each classified independently, and the species assigned by majority vote across segments above a 0.5 confidence threshold.
Ships as a self-contained Docker image and as a Flutter app across four screens: home, live detection, species detail, and history.
Covers 219 species with their endemic region and endangerment status, so a detection returns conservation context rather than a bare label.
Selected as 1 of 80 finalist teams nationally out of the BRIN AIDeaNation 2026 proposal round.
narrative: Passive acoustic monitoring is one of the cheapest ways to track bird populations across large conservation areas, but the output of the research was a model, not something a ranger in Borneo could use. This packages the classifier so it runs offline on a phone, and pairs every detection with the species' endemic region and endangerment status.

title: Bone Metastasis Diagnosis Framework
summary: Open-source bone scan diagnosis pipeline. Patient-level AUC 0.956, above EXINI and BONENAVI, both commercial systems used in clinics today.
highlights: Annotated 600+ whole-body bone scans under nuclear medicine physicians at Dr. Hasan Sadikin Hospital.
Skeletal segmentation with nnU-Net v2 across 12 anatomical regions, feeding automated Bone Scan Index quantification.
Patient-level classification with XGBoost and LightGBM reaching AUC 0.956, above the two commercial systems in clinical use at the time.
Published in Knowledge-Based Systems with code and dataset released open access.
narrative: Staging bone metastasis requires computing a Bone Scan Index from whole-body scintigraphy images, a task currently done by two proprietary commercial systems with no open alternative. This project built a fully open pipeline: annotating scans from scratch under physician supervision, training segmentation models, and quantifying BSI automatically. The goal was clinical-grade accuracy with complete transparency.

title: Driver Behaviour Analysis and Fatigue Detection System
summary: Primary engineer on the production inference service for a mining fleet telematics client. FastAPI, Celery and Redis on a CPU-only VM, handling 40,000 to 50,000 dashcam videos.
highlights: Primary author of the cloud inference service: a three-service FastAPI, Celery and Redis Docker stack on a 4-vCPU CPU-only VM, with a documented API contract and 163 test functions.
Built the data cleaning, labelling and pairing pipeline that turned raw MDVR alarm footage into a 71,129-clip, 85 GB training set across three mining fleets.
Sole author of the real-time Streamlit demonstration app, running landmark extraction at 10 fps with classification over a rolling 20-second buffer.
Wrote the batch inference path: CSV in, per-clip verdicts out, with worker count and device set by environment variable so hardware changes need no code edit.

Built a multimodal fusion variant joining the temporal landmark branch to a 3D-CNN face-crop branch through cross-modal attention, evaluated it across all three fleets, and rejected it: 16 to 22 accuracy points below the landmark-only model at roughly a thousand times the input data per sample.
The 2.39M-parameter model runs entirely on CPU at 9.17 MB, at 700 to 900 MB RAM per worker.
Still running in production as of August 2026, four months after handover.
narrative: TransTrack needed drowsiness verdicts on dashcam alarms from three active mining fleets. The hard part was not the model, it was everything around it: raw MDVR footage arrived duplicated and unlabelled, landmark extraction failed on roughly two thirds of a graded sample, and the service had to answer a push API and call back reliably on infrastructure with no GPU. I built the data pipeline that made the training set usable and the inference service that put it in front of the client.

title: Telplastina: Offline Bone Scintigraphy Workstation
summary: The studies cannot leave the building, the acquisition workstation has restricted network access, and there is no budget for a vendor licence. So it ships as one offline executable that never opens a socket to the outside.
highlights: Four supervised processes on one machine: a Tauri 2 and Rust desktop shell, a Vue 3 interface, a Rust and Axum application server, and a Python and FastAPI inference service, all bound to ephemeral loopback ports.

DICOM import resolves transfer syntax and photometric interpretation, assigns anterior and posterior views from view code sequences with a documented fallback to frame order, and exports results as a DICOM segmentation object.

De-identification removes patient name and birth date instead of writing placeholders, derives a stable pseudonym by hash applied to the stored filename as well as the record, and shifts study dates by a patient-derived offset so intervals between a patient's studies survive.
Multitask nnU-Net with two decoders on a shared encoder, trained on 2,925 paired studies under a fixed patient-level split and evaluated on 293 held out across nine configurations.
Reader correction across 12 skeletal regions and 2 lesion classes with undo, redo, and dirty-rectangle repaint, and a Bone Scan Index computed from masks saved to disk rather than from canvas state.
Cut the offline installer from 1,219 MB to 426 MB by excluding static link libraries never opened at runtime, verified by running identical studies through both bundles and comparing mask pixels.
narrative: Bone Scan Index quantifies skeletal tumour burden as the percentage of the skeleton involved by metastasis. Reading it by hand is slow and varies between observers, and the automated products that exist are commercial, tied to specific scanner vendors, and priced for well funded departments. Every architectural decision here follows from the deployment target: one executable carrying the interface, both backend processes, a Python runtime and the model weights, with a disposable index on disk that can be deleted and rebuilt from the files themselves. The index is a research instrument. Regional weighting is uniform rather than published anatomical weights, so its values are internally consistent and are not comparable to figures reported elsewhere, and the application carries no regulatory clearance.

title: Deep Learning for Bird Sound Identification
summary: 200 endemic and endangered bird species from Indonesia, Malaysia, and Borneo. Trained on jungle recordings, field-tested at zoos in Bandung and Sarawak under uncontrolled noise.
highlights: Fine-tuned BirdNET on 200 endemic and endangered species, raising accuracy from 69.0% to 76.3% and macro F1 from 53.6% to 65.9% on the held-out test set.
Built the dataset from Xeno-canto and PBHAR, including 8,840 negative samples, split by recording to prevent leakage.
Built a first application around the classifier and field-tested it at zoos in Bandung and Sarawak. The model ran on a server, so the app needed a connection.
Results under real noise were mixed, which set the direction for both the follow-on source-separation work and the move to on-device inference.
First author, published at ICITACEE 2025, IEEE Xplore.
narrative: Passive acoustic monitoring is one of the most cost-effective ways to track bird populations across large conservation areas in Southeast Asia, and no existing model was trained on the endemic and endangered species of Indonesia, Malaysia, and Borneo. This built the dataset from scratch and adapted an established model to the regional subset. Testing it at zoos in Bandung and Sarawak exposed the gap between benchmark numbers and real conditions: under uncontrolled noise the results were mixed, and the app depended on a server connection that a forest does not have. Both problems set the direction for what came next.

title: Telrax: Multi-Task Chest X-Ray Analysis Platform
summary: Five AI modules in one CXR system: classification, organ segmentation, report generation, VQA, visual grounding. Ships as both a web app and a desktop app.
highlights: Pathology classification across 14 disease categories, expanding to 20+ aligned to Indonesian Ministry of Health categories. Fine-tuned on VinBig and NIH ChestX-ray14, comparing DenseNet and transformer-based architectures.
Organ segmentation covering right lung, left lung, and heart, outputting masks and annotated overlays from DICOM inputs.
Report generation producing structured clinical findings and impressions from CXR images.
Backend: FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker Compose; AI modules served as microservices.
Interactive report editor with doctor-editable findings, probability bars, and canvas annotation tools.
narrative: Reading a chest X-ray involves multiple simultaneous tasks: identifying pathologies, locating organs, generating a structured report, and answering clinical questions. This project builds a five-module platform where each task is a separate AI module, delivered together as a unified clinical tool for radiologist-assisted diagnosis.

title: Provider-Aware Contrastive Learning for B2B Travel Inventory
summary: Four providers, 3.69 million accommodation records, and a five-star rating that means something different depending on who sent it. 1st Winner, ICoICT 2026 Challenge.
highlights: Trained a contrastive encoder on 3.69 million accommodation records from RateHawk, Expedia, Agoda, and HotelBeds, learning from destination and quality-tier co-membership where no verified property links existed.
Masked provider identity during training so the embedding stops encoding which supplier a listing came from, then measured how well providers mix in each property's neighbourhood.
Introduced a new evaluation protocol for settings where verified cross-provider links are unavailable, and reported it as a representation result rather than claiming a ranking improvement.
Outperformed every alignment baseline tested, including CORAL, MMD, and gradient reversal.
First place in the ICoICT 2026 Challenge track, accepted as a first-author IEEE paper.
narrative: B2B travel platforms resell the same hotel through several providers, and each provider grades quality on its own scale, so a five-star listing from one supplier is not the same product as a five-star listing from another. One provider in this dataset supplied over half the inventory but a small fraction of the bookings. With no verified links between listings of the same physical property, this trains on a weaker signal, destination and tier co-membership, and measures success by how well providers mix in the neighbourhood of each property.

title: VLM-Based Chest X-Ray Anomaly Explanation
summary: Grad-CAM tells you where the model looked. This system tells you what it found, in words a radiologist can actually use.
highlights: Three-module pipeline: anomaly detection, visual-text alignment, and structured clinical report generation.
Explanation quality evaluated directly by radiologists on a 100-case gold-standard subset, not only BLEU or BERTScore.
Target: external clinical validation and integration into radiology reporting workflows.

title: Gated Mixture-of-Experts Fusion for Multimodal Deepfake Detection
institution: Telkom University · AI Lab Focused Group
summary: Every segment reports which modality caught the fake. Audio-video forgeries route to the audio expert, video-only forgeries to the visual expert. Runs faster than real time on a consumer laptop GPU. Accepted at ICoDSA 2026.
highlights: A Modality Reliability Gate routes each 2-second segment to an audio or visual expert based on learned anomaly scores from frozen VideoMAE and Whisper encoders.
The gate reports which modality drove each verdict, a forensic signal none of the compared methods produce.
Accuracy matches static fusion rather than beating it. The contribution is interpretability and speed, and the paper says so plainly.
Ranking quality survives moving to unseen datasets, though the fixed decision threshold does not, which the paper reports as a limitation.
Trained across PolyglotFake, FakeAVCeleb, HiDF, CelebDFv2, and FF++, split at subject level to prevent leakage.
Analyses a 2-minute video in around 24 seconds on an RTX 4050 laptop GPU.
narrative: Most audio-visual detectors assume both channels are equally corrupted. They break when only one is: a face-swapped video with genuine audio, or synthesised speech over real footage. This project built a gate that decides per segment which modality to trust, and reports that decision as a number a forensic analyst can read. The accuracy matches static fusion rather than beating it; what static fusion cannot do is tell you why it decided.

title: Sentiment Analysis Classification: Multi-Class Text
summary: Multi-class text sentiment classifier (positive, neutral, negative) built as a final project for the CCI Data Research Division.
highlights: Compared LSTM, GRU, BERT, LightGBM, XGBoost, and CatBoost on the same dataset.
Achieved 70% accuracy, improved iteratively through embedding and architecture experiments.

title: Retogen: Article Management Platform
summary: Full-stack web platform for publishing and moderating tech-review articles, built as a production-grade system with complete test coverage.
highlights: JWT authentication with user and admin roles; full article lifecycle including image upload with format validation.
Hierarchical nested comments and 1–5 star ratings.
185 automated tests covering authentication, CRUD operations, and edge cases.

title: Anothem: Desktop AI Storytelling Engine
summary: Local LLM desktop application for AI-assisted creative writing, designed to run entirely on consumer hardware with no cloud dependency.
highlights: Runs multiple local LLMs, including a custom recurrent model, entirely on consumer hardware with no cloud required.
Token-streamed UI with background incremental summarization to maintain context across long writing sessions.
Auto-detects narrative intent (description, dialogue, scene) and injects appropriate writing guidance per generation.

title: Real-Time AR Face Filter App
summary: Browser-based augmented reality app demonstrating live face-tracking overlays, developed to increase engagement for a local UMKM churos business.
highlights: Runs at 10 FPS on Streamlit Cloud with no local installation: face detection and 3 animated overlays.
WebRTC live video with server-side overlay compositing applied per frame.
Pure OpenCV pipeline for zero native library dependencies on Streamlit Cloud.
